discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 071639
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
1239 PM EDT Wed Oct 7 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dry and pleasant weather continues through Saturday with 
  highs generally in the 70s and lows in the mid 40s to low 50s.

- The next chance of rain arrives on Sunday associated with the
  remnants of a tropical system. No significant impacts are
  expected with this event.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 113 AM EDT Wed Oct 7 2026

Quiet weather to persist through the end of the week. A 130+ kt 
upper level jet and attendant PV anomaly passes through the Great 
Lakes later today. However, we remain in the unfavorable right exit 
region of this jet streak. Better CVA also passes to the north and 
lags well behind the associated surface front. Modest return flow 
ahead of this front will push highs near 80F (particularly in our 
S/SW) but surface dewpoints remain in the 50s and forecast soundings 
show very dry/stable and capped profiles. No precip expected with 
this frontal passage and likely just some high-based clouds at times 
through tonight. Another broad low level anticyclone then settles 
into the Upper Midwest on Thursday on the downstream side of large 
western CONUS ridge. Highs on Thu drop back to around 70F with 
dewpoints around 40F. Surface high passes over our area Thu night 
and return flow starts again by late Friday. Several deterministic 
00Z models generate some light QPF along the associated warm front/ 
theta-e surge but NBM is holding dry. Wouldn't be surprised if we 
have to add a low chance PoP or sprinkle mention Fri night but will 
hold off for now.

Attention then turns to the remnants of what will likely become 
Hurricane Isaias in the Gulf over the next few days. Latest 00Z 
guidance showing a westward shift in the associated rain shield that 
now clips much of our area with at least some light rain on Sunday. 
NBM PoP's now over 60% for much of our SE CWA. Still not expecting 
any appreciable impacts from this event though. Even a widespread 1-
1.5" should be tolerable given recent dry conditions and that is 
definitely on the high-end of possible outcomes. QPF amounts could 
easily be much lower. Some breezy conditions also possible but again 
not strong enough to be impactful.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z THURSDAY/...
Issued at 1237 PM EDT Wed Oct 7 2026

High pressure continues to provide tranquil and dry conditions.
Expect VFR ceilings through the TAF period (with very few 
clouds at all) with west winds between 5-10 knots. There could
still be a few gusts this afternoon to 20 kts along and east of
I-69, but otherwise, winds will be relaxing this evening and
overnight.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...AGD
AVIATION...Johnson

spc.text:
SPC AC 071620

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1120 AM CDT Wed Oct 07 2026

   Valid 071630Z - 081200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Organized severe thunderstorms are unlikely across the contiguous
   United States through tonight.

   ...Central portion of the Florida Peninsula...
   A diffuse frontal zone modulated by scattered showers and isolated
   thunderstorm activity will remain draped over the central portion of
   the FL Peninsula through tonight.  A very moist tropospheric profile
   (sampled by the 12 UTC Tampa Bay raob) featuring weak lapse rates
   will limit overall updraft strength with scattered convection this
   afternoon across the Peninsula.  Weak flow (at or below 20 kt) from
   surface through 300 mb will also act to restrict storm organization
   potential.  Although a brief tornado/waterspout near the coast
   cannot be ruled out, it appears the risk for transient supercell
   structures and an associated threat for a brief tornado appear
   sufficiently low to preclude introducing severe probabilities this
   outlook update.

   ...Northern New York...
   Isolated low-topped thunderstorms will be possible late today and
   more so into tonight, influenced by an amplifying upstream
   upper-level trough and approaching cold front.  Overall buoyancy
   will be limited, but still sufficient for the possibility of
   thunderstorms.  Furthermore, some convective enhancement/gusty winds
   are plausible tonight given the increasing magnitude of the
   low/mid-tropospheric flow and steepening lapse rates atop the
   boundary layer.

   ..Smith/Barnes.. 10/07/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

spc.text:
SPC AC 071715

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1215 PM CDT Wed Oct 07 2026

   Valid 081200Z - 091200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   The risk of severe thunderstorms appears low across the U.S. for
   Thursday through Thursday night.

   ...Discussion...
   A generally zonal belt of stronger westerlies is likely to persist
   into and through this period across the northern mid-latitudes of
   North America.  Within this regime, broad mid/upper troughing is
   forecast to continue shifting east of the lower Great Lakes through
   the northern Atlantic Seaboard.  Forcing for ascent associated with
   an embedded short wave trough may support renewed cyclogenesis
   across eastern Quebec through Newfoundland and Labrador, with an
   initial trailing cold front advancing offshore of much of the
   northern through middle Atlantic Seaboard by late Thursday night.  

   Upstream, cyclogenesis also appears likely to the lee of the
   Canadian Rockies, in advance of larger-scale mid/upper troughing
   digging across and inland of the British Columbia coast.  It appears
   that this will be accompanied by deepening surface troughing to the
   lee of the northern U.S. Rockies, through much of the northern and
   central Great Plains, by 12Z Friday.

   High boundary-layer moisture content remains confined to the
   southern mid- to subtropical latitudes, and is not likely to
   appreciably return northward.  However, a corridor of modest
   low-level moisture may linger along a stalling to northward
   returning segment of the frontal zone across the central Great
   Plains into middle to lower Missouri Valley.  Even so, latest model
   output suggests that this will probably remain capped by warm, dry
   air in the lower/mid-troposphere, with little support for the
   initiation of thunderstorms, aside from, perhaps, better moisture
   return within a corridor of strengthening lower/mid-level warm
   advection across Iowa late Thursday night into early Friday.

   In the wake of the initial surface cold front, across parts of the
   lower Great Lakes region into northern New England, fairly
   significant cooling in the 700-500 mb layer may be sufficient to
   contribute to scattered, generally weak, thunderstorm activity.

   In lower-latitudes, convection-allowing guidance suggests that
   modestly cool mid-levels, in the wake of digging upper-level
   troughing across the southern Rockies and Great Plains, may
   contribute to scattered diurnal thunderstorm development across
   parts of the Four Corner's states into Rio Grande Valley.

   Downstream of the digging upper troughing, and a potentially
   strengthening hurricane (Isaias) slowly migrating northeastward
   across the southwestern Gulf Basin, scattered thunderstorm activity
   will remain possible within the lingering high moisture content air
   near northeastern Gulf coastal areas, and across portions of the
   Florida Peninsula, Thursday through Thursday night.

   ..Kerr.. 10/07/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0600Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 070734

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0234 AM CDT Wed Oct 07 2026

   Valid 091200Z - 101200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ALONG THE
   NORTH-CENTRAL GULF COAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   An increasing tornado risk may develop into early Saturday morning
   along the north-central Gulf Coast in association with the
   developing tropical cyclone.

   ...Discussion...
   Severe storm chances will be low across most of the CONUS on Friday,
   the exception being over the northern Gulf Coast late Friday night
   into Saturday morning.

   NHC currently forecasts Tropical Depression 9 to become a hurricane
   late Thursday, strengthening further into Friday over the Gulf of
   America. Some uncertainty exists as to the timing of an eventual
   forward acceleration northward. In any case, the system is forecast
   to affect the northern Gulf Coast late in the Day 3 period (which
   ends at 12Z Saturday morning), and as such, low probabilities for
   tornado risk have been added.

   Low-level shear/SRH will be very strong east of the storm center.
   The surface air mass may remain stable over the mainland until very
   close to 12Z Saturday, with a greater chance of larger SBCAPE over
   extreme southeast LA prior to 12Z. Once the coastal boundary moves
   inland, a surge of mid 70s F dewpoints and southerly winds will lead
   to overly enlarged hodographs, supporting rotation in the stronger
   cells with tornado potential.

   ..Jewell.. 10/07/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
